newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast says merger fast-tracks growth.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast says merger fast-tracks growth.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc pursued a major natural gas and electicity marketing merger with Coastal Corp because it offered the size and scope not available inside its own operation, Westcoast president and chief operating officer Art Willms said on Tuesday.
"We had been growing it within but it's very slow and very difficult, so this is a quantum leap for us," Willms said in a telephone interview from Vancouver.
Vancouver-based Westcoast and Coastal of Houston on Tuesday announced a widely anticipated merger of their gas and power marketing operations.

The deal, which gained widespread analyst approval in reports leading up to the announcement, creates North America's fourth largest marketer of gas and electricity with daily volumes of seven billion cubic feet.
The merger would create a new entity in which the parent companies would own 50 percent each.
The firms' boards approved the deal in principle, subject to more due diligence and completion of definitive agreements, they said.
Willms said he did not expect many staff to lose their jobs as a result of the merger.
Westcoast currently employs about 120 in its Calgary-based Westcoast Gas Services arm and Coastal has about 220 gas marketing staff in its unit.
"We anticipate very limited attrition on this thing," he said. "This is a company that's going to be growing rather than going into a cost-cutting mode."
Most of the gas sold and traded by the new company will be done on a third-party basis, he said.
Willms said Coast's exploration and production arm had aggressive plans to boost its output beyond the current 400 MMCFD over the next few years.
All the production is slated to be sold by the merged marketing firm.
Willms said that while small niche marketers would likely continue to play a role in the North American gas industry, the move to so-called megamarketers was set to maintain its brisk pace.
Other major recent deals include mergers between NGC Corp and Chevron Corp, as well as PanEnergy Corp and Mobil Corp.
Shell Canada Ltd said on Monday it was joining major marketer Coral Energy, which would sell its 800 million cubic feet per day of gas production.

"Because of decreasing margins and so on, you will see significant combiniations like this, and they will not only sell natural gas but, as we point out, electricity and other energy sources," Willms said. "You'll see full-service energy providers."
He said the deal announced on Tuesday did not include the bringing of gas plants, gathering systems and storage facilities -- so-called midstream assets -- into the merged entity.
Willms declined to discuss Westcoast's financial projections as a result of the merger. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
